relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: David gathers military, tribal, economic, court, and property leadership around succession.
He stands and names the temple dream he prepared.
The warrior king repeats that bloodshed disqualifies him from building the sanctuary.
He interprets his rise through a narrowing sequence of chosen tribe, house, and son.
Solomon is selected from many sons to sit on a throne called Divine.
The young heir receives father-son covenant and construction duty.
The promise remains conditional on justice and commandment.
The public is charged to seek Torah while land inheritance is placed before future children.
Solomon is told that no thought is hidden, language that must never become human surveillance.
Chosen duty becomes the command to be strong and act.
David hands over architectural patterns for every royal-sacred chamber.
The design is attributed to spirit and extends through courts and treasuries.
People, schedules, work, and vessels are incorporated into the plan.
Gold and silver are weighed service by service.
Even lamps and stands receive material specifications.
Tables are assigned precious metals by function.
Utensils and bowls are included in the wealth of the design.
The incense altar and cherubim-chariot receive refined gold.
David presents the whole pattern as written insight from YHWH.
He promises Divine presence until the work is complete.
Skilled willing workers stand ready, yet the final phrase places them under royal command.

contemplative_note: A spiritual vision becomes architecture only through money, measurements, engineering, and human work. Claiming a plan came from Spirit increases responsibility; it does not eliminate review. The sacred blueprint must remain answerable to safety, access, consent, budget, and the workers whose hands turn vision into structure.
